subject.title: feat: standalone embeddable thread view with opt-in frame origins

question: Should ClickClack core support arbitrary cross-origin authenticated thread embeds with normal session cookies, or should the first supported contract be limited to same-site trusted hosts until a dedicated embed-auth design exists?
rationale: The PR adds a new CSP allowlist and promises cookie-authenticated embedding, but browser third-party-cookie policy makes the long-term cross-site authentication behavior a product and security-boundary decision rather than a mechanical implementation detail.

options.title: Constrain the first release to same-site hosts
options.body: Document and test that configured embedding hosts must be same-site with ClickClack, preserving the existing session-cookie model without promising behavior browsers may block.

options.title: Design explicit cross-site embed authentication
options.body: Keep arbitrary cross-origin framing as a supported capability only after defining a dedicated, narrowly scoped embed authentication and privacy model.

options.title: Defer the embedding feature
options.body: Pause the core feature until maintainers choose whether this capability belongs in ClickClack core and approve its browser-auth contract.

recommendation.title: Constrain the first release to same-site hosts
recommendation.body: Document and test that configured embedding hosts must be same-site with ClickClack, preserving the existing session-cookie model without promising behavior browsers may block.
